children: Communication services stocks have been navigating a mixed environment as advertising demand, wireless subscriber trends and corporate spending on digital platforms continue to shape the sector.

Advertising-driven companies remain exposed to shifts in marketing budgets and digital ad demand, while wireless operators and communications providers face competitive pressures, capital requirements and changing consumer usage patterns.
Against this backdrop, a quantitative screen finds only two Communication Services stocks that have maintained a Sell or Strong Sell Quant Rating for at least 60 consecutive days.
The list is topped by Gogo Inc.
, which has maintained a Strong Sell Quant Rating for 376 consecutive days. The Trade Desk, Inc.

follows with 66 consecutive days at a Strong Sell rating. The two companies represent different parts of the sector, with Gogo operating in wireless telecommunications services and The Trade Desk in advertising.

The limited number of qualifying stocks makes this one of the narrower sector screens, with just two Communication Services companies sustaining a Sell or Strong Sell rating for more than two months. Gogo has maintained the rating for more than a year, while The Trade Desk has remained at Strong Sell for more than two months.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and price momentum relative to their sector peers.
